title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Their Château Miraval Dispute
excerpt: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have agreed to dismiss their claims against each other over Château Miraval. Pitt’s separate claims against the buyer of Jolie’s stake remain unresolved.
seo_title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Miraval Lawsuit
seo_description: Pitt and Jolie reach a confidential out-of-court settlement over their French winery, while Pitt continues pursuing claims against the buyer of Jolie’s stake.
body_md:
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have reached an out-of-court settlement in their longstanding dispute concerning Château Miraval, the French winery they previously owned together. The Hollywood Reporter reported on November 25, 2026, that both sides had moved to dismiss their claims against one another. The financial and legal terms of their agreement have not been disclosed.

In a joint statement, representatives for the former couple said the settlement was reached in the interests of their family. They also indicated that neither party intended to comment further and rejected the suggestion that anonymous remarks attributed to sources in media coverage came from them or people close to them.

## The dispute over the winery

Pitt and Jolie acquired the property in southern France in 2008. It subsequently became the location of their wedding. After their relationship ended, negotiations over the possible transfer of Jolie's share to Pitt broke down. Court filings identified a proposed nondisclosure agreement as a point of disagreement during those talks.

Jolie subsequently agreed to sell her interest in the winery in a transaction valued at $64 million involving businessman Yuri Shefler. Pitt filed a lawsuit in 2022, alleging that the sale violated an unwritten agreement requiring each partner to secure the other's consent before transferring their stake. That allegation was contested as part of the litigation.

## Allegations raised during the case

Jolie's countersuit included allegations of abusive behavior by Pitt during a private flight in 2016 involving the former couple and their children. A representative for Pitt denied the allegations when they became public. The FBI investigated the incident, but criminal charges were not filed.

The settlement should not be interpreted as a judicial determination of the truth of those allegations. The report does not identify any admission of wrongdoing by either party or disclose terms that would support such a conclusion.

## Litigation involving the buyer remains open

The agreement resolves the claims between Pitt and Jolie, but it does not bring every aspect of the Miraval litigation to a conclusion. According to the report, Pitt is continuing to pursue claims against Shefler and Tenute del Mondo. His requested remedies include an opportunity to purchase Jolie's former interest at the valuation used in the transaction, along with damages.

The distinction is important: the former couple have ended their direct legal dispute, while litigation involving other parties remains outstanding. No settlement payment or final resolution of those remaining claims has been made public in the report.
